disclaimer: BloodIQ is educational and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional about your lab results.

implementation_notes.Reference ranges: Use the reference range printed on the user's laboratory report whenever available. Do not hard-code one universal range for all users.
implementation_notes.Units: Store the original reported unit. Normalize units only when the conversion is validated and the analyte is truly comparable.
implementation_notes.Aliases: Map aliases to a standard biomarker ID while retaining the original extracted test name for traceability.
implementation_notes.Status: For ordinary numeric tests: value < reference_low = LOW; value > reference_high = HIGH; otherwise NORMAL. Handle missing/open-ended ranges explicitly.
implementation_notes.Trend analysis: Compare measurements only when the standardized biomarker, analyte subtype, and units are compatible.
implementation_notes.Calculated biomarkers: Non-HDL cholesterol and transferrin saturation may be calculated when required inputs are available; retain whether the value was reported or calculated.
implementation_notes.Special analytes: RDW subtypes, reticulocyte count formats, vitamin D analytes, calcium types, CRP types, and folate types must not be silently merged.
implementation_notes.Safety: BloodIQ is educational. It must not diagnose, prescribe treatment, or replace professional medical advice.
